title: GPU NodeGroup Autoscaling Composer module for Private VPC (ASG + Karpenter orchestration)
creator: Liam Chen
description: Design and implement a reusable Terraform module ("gpu-nodegroup-autoscaling-composer") for Private VPC deployments that composes ASG-based GPU nodegroups and Karpenter provisioners. Goal: give platform teams a single module to declare GPU capacity intent and a safe, observable runtime that supports upgrades, mixed spot/on-demand pools, health checks, and graceful fallback between ASG and Karpenter. Module must be production-ready for Private customers with strict network constraints and KMS-backed secrets.
implementation_notes: High-level approach: keep two primary submodules (ASG and Karpenter-provisioner) and a lightweight orchestration layer that wires IAM, launch templates, taints/tolerations, and node labeling. Provide switchable 'primary' policy so a customer can prefer ASG or Karpenter for stable workloads and fallback to the other if capacity constrained. Implement driver/OS upgrade hooks, node draining hooks, and a healthcheck suite that exposes Prometheus metrics and CloudWatch-style alarms via module outputs. Use policy: minimal breaking surface for existing infra — default to conservative instance types and explicit allowlists for GPU SKUs. Provide example root module for private clusters with S3-backed bootstrap artifacts and optional private registry for GPU drivers.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module published to internal registry with semver v0.1.0
Can deploy mixed capacity (spot + on-demand) with configurable fallback policy
Automated healthchecks: node readiness probe, daemonset GPU-driver status, and alerting outputs documented
Upgrade process documented and tested in staging: driver + k8s node OS rollouts with pre-checks and canary option
IAM least-privilege templates for both ASG and Karpenter provisioner included
E2E smoke tests pass in staging cluster using the provided example root module
Module passes security review (KMS integration, no plaintext secrets in state outputs)

notes_on_tradeoffs: We chose composition over a single monolithic module to minimize blast radius when upgrading provider logic (ASG vs Karpenter).
Running a lightweight watcher/controller adds operational overhead but gives deterministic fallback behavior without requiring customers to run custom automation.
Prefer injecting a small set of explicit variables rather than relying on wide discovery of instance types to keep module predictable across private VPCs.
Support for mixed spot/on-demand will require documented operator guidance on acceptable eviction policies for model-serving pods — we won't try to fully automate eviction-safe bin-packing in v0.1.0.
We will not enable automatic driver upgrades by default; the module exposes hooks and a documented canary path so customers can opt in after testing.
